title: Limit of a Function
topicTitle: Limits and continuity: limits of a function, indeterminate forms, algebraic properties of limits (without proof), basic theorems on limits of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
notes: **Definition of limit:** $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$ means that as $x$ approaches $a$ (but $x \neq a$), the value of $f(x)$ approaches $L$.

**One-sided limits:** The left-hand limit $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x)$ considers values of $x$ less than $a$; the right-hand limit $\lim_{x \to a^+} f(x)$ considers values greater than $a$. For the limit to exist, both one-sided limits must be equal.
**Existence of a limit:** $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$ exists if and only if $\lim_{x \to a^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to a^+} f(x) = L$.

**Geometric interpretation:** On the graph of $y = f(x)$, the limit $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$ means the $y$-value approaches $L$ as the curve is traced toward $x = a$ from both sides. The function need not be defined at $x = a$ itself.

**Physical interpretation:** If $f(t)$ represents position at time $t$, then $\lim_{t \to a} f(t)$ gives the position approached at time $a$, regardless of whether the object is actually at that position.
confusion: The limit $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ does NOT require $f(a)$ to exist. The limit is about the behaviour of $f(x)$ near $a$, not at $a$.
Do not substitute $x = a$ directly as a first step — many limits yield $0/0$ which requires algebraic simplification before substitution.
practice: Find the left-hand and right-hand limits of $f(x) = |x|/x$ as $x \to 0$ and determine whether the limit exists.
Sketch a function where the left-hand and right-hand limits exist but are not equal.
universalFacts: Limits are the foundation of all calculus — derivatives and integrals are both defined via limits.
The concept of a limit extends naturally to sequences: $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = L$ means the sequence values approach $L$.
